lines.text: Have you seen a goose? White. Mean. Answers to Mrs. Applegate.
I was to bring her to the fair, to be shown. She showed me. She went up the orchard road with her neck out.
She bit the minister. Mama says that's not a reason to lose her.
The orchard. I'll keep an eye out, Tilly.
I'm not crying. It's the wind. It's a very big wind.
The orchard, I think. Mind her. She goes for the knees.
A large white goose stands in the windfalls, eating a rotten apple with an air of having paid for it. She looks up, and her neck comes out.
Mrs. Applegate. Forgive the intrusion. There's a young woman on the Green who is very much in want of you.
The goose hisses. Then, as though it were her own idea, she turns downhill.
I can see why the minister gave way.

banner: Walking home, on her own terms

lines.text: Mrs. Applegate is on the Green already, as if she had never been anywhere else. Tilly has both arms round her. The goose bears it.
She came back! I knew she would. I told everybody.
She walked the whole way herself. I was only going in the same direction.
Here. These are my peppermints. I was saving them for if she died. And this is some of her. It came off by itself.
She didn't win. The judge said she has a poor attitude. Mrs. Applegate bit him, so now they're even.
Mrs. Applegate looks Eldwin slowly up and down, and settles on the knee. He moves along.
Tilly is sitting on the mossy stones where the path goes out to the road, with something wound round her hand.
She went up the road this morning. With her neck out.
Geese go south. I told her. She went the other way.
She does like to make up her own mind.
Mama says you're going that way.
I am.
Then this is for her. It was on my Sunday dress. I'll tell Mama after.
A blue ribbon, still creased where it was tied.
She likes the left side of the road. Don't let her have cheese. She'll want it.
Left side. No cheese.
Will you bring her back?
Mrs. Applegate goes where she likes. I'll be glad of the company while she does.
Go on, then. She'll be miles ahead.

gear.line: Blue, off a Sunday dress. Still creased where it was tied.

lines.text: Tilly is sitting on the mossy stones where the path goes out to the road, watching the road.
Mama says she'll come home when she's hungry.
She's always hungry. So.
If you see a goose, she's white, and she bites. That's her.
I'll know her.
Tell her I left the gate open.
If I see her, I'll tell her.
She goes back to watching the road.
